title: Example manifest
description: Derived from design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.2 (Draft); the document wins. Draft: ARIADNE specifies this format and Tillman Heisner freezes its version (section 1.3; D9 A). One example manifest (section 3.3), per agent, condition and fold, so that agents keep separate examples and leave-one-out holds.
$comment: Derived from design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.2 (Draft); the document wins. Section 3.3 gives the fields, and the list-level fields follow section 3 (List-level fields); the key name files inside an example is proposed. Checksums are lowercase (section 3). Of the manifest check of section 3.3, this file expresses rule 2 (a zero-shot manifest lists no example, examples: []) and the part of rule 4 that one manifest shows: the fold is required in both conditions and is dev-T9HQ4X, dev-GNICYO or test; there is no fold all, and a zero-shot manifest has the fold of the items that use it, one per agent and fold. Not expressed here: rules 1, 3, 5 and 6 of the check (sources, reviews, checksums, agent, canaries and expected-side keys), and of rule 4 that no example comes from the protected side of leave-one-out and that every item using the manifest has its fold, in either condition (section 3.4), which need other files. The examples are illustrative: ids, times, checksums, sizes, counts and names are made up.

example_manifest_id.description: Id, quoted in packet manifests and evaluation run records.

evaluation_interfaces_version.description: The version of design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md the list follows (section 3, List-level fields).

frozen_on.description: The date Tillman Heisner froze it; absent while it is a draft (section 3).

fold.description: Required in both conditions: dev-T9HQ4X, dev-GNICYO or test, equal to the fold of every item that uses the manifest (section 3.3). There is no other value.

source_id.description: T9HQ4X, GNICYO, or a variant of either.

files.description: Proposed name. The example files with their SHA-256.

examples.description: Empty ([]) for zero-shot; at least one reviewed example for few-shot (section 3.3).

checksum.description: A checksum: the SHA-256 of a file's exact bytes as stored, 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, computed by software (Run records 1.2 and 2.9; Evaluation interfaces, section 3).
